question: Where is the Ashoka Pillar Lion located? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Sanchi
Sarnath
Pataliputra
Mehrauli
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sarnath

Explanation:
The Ashoka Pillar Lion is located in Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh. This pillar was erected by Emperor Ashoka around 250 BCE. The capital of the pillar features four lions seated back-to-back on a pedestal, which is the National Emblem of India. The pillar also bears an inscription forbidding the division of the Buddhist sangha. Sarnath is the place where Gautam Buddha gave his first sermon. The Ashoka Pillar Lion was adopted as the National Emblem of India and is a significant symbol of Indian heritage.

This waterfall is a nationally significant natural site and a popular tourist destination.

question: The world's highest peak is? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Kanchanganga Mountains
Kilimanjaro Mountains
Salad Mountain
Mount Everest
solution:

Explanation:
Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world, with an elevation of 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 feet) above sea level. It is located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and Tibet (China). question: Which of the following star is closest to the sun? (RPF Constable 2018 (17/01/2019) Shift 3)
options: Apasti
Huntsman
Swati
Proxima Centauri
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Proxima Centauri

Explanation:
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to the Sun, located about 4.246 light-years from Earth. It is part of the Alpha Centauri triple star system and is a red dwarf star. Its mass is about 12% of the Sun's mass, and it is particularly studied by astronomers due to its small size. At least one exoplanet (Proxima Centauri b) has been discovered orbiting it, which may lie in the habitable zone. Other options: Apaati (Sirius), Huntsman (Sirius, eight light-years away), and Swati (Arcturus) are farther from the Sun.

question: What is the situation when the sun is vertically above the Tropic Of Cancer? (RPF Constable 2018 (18/02/2019))

Equinox
Summer Solstice
December Sankranti
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Summer Solstice

Explanation:
When the sun is vertically above the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N), it is called the Summer Solstice. It occurs on June 21 and marks the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. On this day, the sun's rays fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer, resulting in maximum temperature and daylight duration in the Northern Hemisphere. Conversely, the Southern Hemisphere experiences its shortest day. The Winter Solstice occurs on December 22 when the sun is over the Tropic of Capricorn, causing the shortest day in the Northern Hemisphere. Equinoxes occur when the sun is vertically above the Equator, happening on March 21 and September 23, resulting in equal day and night globally.

question: The outermost layer or shell of the earth is known as _______. (RPF Constable 2018 (18/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Mantle
Crust
Core
Atmosphere
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Crust

Explanation:
The outermost solid layer of the Earth is called the Crust. It forms the Earth's surface and varies in thickness from about 30-50 km under continents to 5-10 km under oceans. The crust is composed mainly of silica and aluminum (sial) or silica and magnesium (sima). Below the crust lies the Mantle, which is about 2900 km thick. The innermost part is the Core, composed mainly of iron and nickel. The crust is the thinnest layer of the Earth and is considered the upper part of the Lithosphere.

☛ What is the crust and upper mantle together called? → Lithosphere
